card: Speeds up Python functional tests by triggering immediate wakeups in P2PInterface wait_until on message delivery or connection changes rather than polling every 50ms, and by setting noban_tx_relay on relevant tests. This eliminates avoidable idle time for developers and CI running the functional test suite. The author reports a 17.5% reduction in accumulated test runtime and an 11% decrease in total wall time, with some long-running tests dropping by over 80%.
evidence: Author's benchmarks report overall test suite wall time reduced by 11% (110.8s to 99.1s with -j=18) and accumulated runtime reduced by 17.5% (1715s to 1411s)
Significant runtime decreases on individual tests reported in the PR description, including feature_maxuploadtarget (57.9s down to 6.2s) and wallet_conflicts (49.2s down to 7.0s)
problem: Functional test suites waste wall-clock and CPU time waiting on fixed 50ms polling loops in P2PInterface and default tx-relay throttling in individual tests, slowing down local development and CI runs.

risk.why: A flaw in wait_until notification logic could cause test flakiness or false timeouts in CI.

scope_notes: Small patch (+19/-1) touching the functional test framework and several test scripts.
summary: Speeds up functional test execution by waking P2PInterface `wait_until` loops immediately upon message receipt or connection state changes instead of polling on a 50ms timer. It also enables `noban_tx_relay` across tests that can bypass transaction relay delays.
uncertainties: Diff was not provided in the prompt, so specific test framework notification primitives cannot be verified directly.
